title: Corner lot subdivision: reduced setback to the original secondary street
text: C3.3.2 Notwithstanding C3.3.1, the following reductions are permitted: iii. in areas coded R15 or higher, the street setback, may be reduced to 2.5m, or 1.5m to a porch, balcony, verandah or the equivalent, where a single house results from a subdivision of an original corner lot and has its frontage to the original secondary street.

replaces.note: only the single-house corner-lot limb carried (C4P1-080)

verified.note: Wording confirmed on p30: the apartments chapter still says 'where a single house results from a subdivision of an original corner lot'. The page gives no route for an apartment development to qualify (register C4P1-080).

notes: from: ch3 C3.3.2(iii). As printed (p30) the reduction applies only 'where a single house results from a subdivision of an original corner lot', so it cannot reach an apartment development; copied from Chapters 2 and 3 (C4P1-080: not relevant to apartments). Encoded unchanged; a MEETS here should not be relied on for apartments until clarified. The original secondary street is the lot's primary street after subdivision, so the primary street setback fact is tested. The porch limb is C3.3.2(iii)#r1.
